messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — onboarding call with FinServX flagged a 'guaranteed burst' ask. Need a product decision: contract headroom vs autoscale fallback. TL;DR: they'd pay for 3x burst for first 2 months. What are tradeoffs?

Maya R: Quick clarifying Qs — do we have target SLO numbers and expected burst shape? @Irene L did Sales capture exact latency/peak?

Irene L: They want <=150ms p50 for chat, steady 5k concurrent sessions, and the ability to spike to ~15k rps for ~10 minutes/hour. Willing to pay ~20% premium. Asked explicitly for no preemption during their designated peak windows.

Tom B: Infra reality check: preemption-free burst is expensive. Options: 1) Dedicated burst buffer (reserve nodes) — highest cost but simplest guarantees. 2) Prioritized warm spare nodes with soft preemption — cheaper, some risk. 3) Autoscale with very fast warmups + graceful degraded fallback (quantized model or lower context). Warmup for full model typically 90–120s.

Sanjay P: Runtime notes — KV cache priming and prefix snapshot restore can cut warmup a lot. If we snapshot a primed KV cache + warmed kernels we can restore in ~20s for same model variant, but snapshot artifacts are large (~GBs) and require disk-backed storage + orchestration to mount. Also mixing quantized fallback reduces quality for some prompts.

Alex K: So tradeoffs: cost vs startup latency vs ops complexity vs quality. Proposal: offer a "Burst Contract" pilot with: X guaranteed burst minutes/month, 5m warmup SLA (customer pays premium), explicit fallbacks (if warmup fails, degrade to quantized variant). Need launch criteria and spec.

Maya R: Draft launch criteria suggestion: (a) snapshot-restore + prioritized pool implemented end-to-end; (b) billing & usage metering per burst; (c) e2e synthetic load test representing FinServX pattern; (d) quality regression <=5% vs baseline for supported prompts; (e) legal reviewed contract clause about non-preemption windows.

Tom B: Implementation paths: MVP manual route — create a small dedicated pool for pilot + manual ops handoff (2 sprints). Full infra route — snapshot orchestration + automated prioritized pool + preemption policy (6 sprints). Both need billing shim to split usage.

Irene L: FinServX wants GA in ~6 weeks. If we can run the manual pool pilot with an ops SLA we can close the deal. They're okay with a pilot contract that includes outage carve-outs.

Sanjay P: Quick spike options: we can prototype snapshot restore (target ~20s) and an automated priming job. I'll need a ticket and storage for snapshot artifacts. If spike succeeds, we can move to automation path.

Alex K: Action items: Maya — own the product spec + contract wording; Tom — prototype manual-capacity pilot and billing shim; Sanjay — spike snapshot restore (20s target) and report feasibility; Irene — set customer expectations and draft pilot offer. Sync tomorrow 10:30 to align.

deploy-bot: New ticket created — INC-4321: spike/snapshot-restore-prototype assigned to @Sanjay P.

Maya R: I'll open the spec PR and loop in Legal for the non-preemption clause. Also adding a short checklist to the PR for launch criteria and observability events (burst_start, burst_end, warmup_time, fallback_used).

Tom B: Note for infra: monitoring needs to capture pool headroom by tenant and a per-burst cost estimator so Sales can show projected bill. I'll add a quick dashboard mock for tomorrow.

Alex K: Thanks — try to keep the pilot small and measurable. We'll iterate policy after pilot metrics.
